## Details

<a id="disk_protection"></a>
### [`disk_protection`](../../../../src/leftovers/leftover_393d.asm#L6) `$393D`

*routine*

Disk protection, reached from op 9 of the start-up script at $1def ($0a81 runs that script; the Mayday! release has 3 NOPs at $0955, so nothing calls $0a81). A RAM test at $8413: when the byte does not keep $01 and $00, protection_failed. Then it sets the KERNAL IRQ and NMI vectors ($2c45) and reads 2 blocks of track 33 into the buffer of channel 5. For each block it opens the buffer channel (protection_open_buffer), sends a B-R command with $2c83 (OPEN and CLOSE of channel 15) and reads the drive status (drive_status: C clear for 00). Sector 5 must give a drive error, sector 6 must give no error. A failed check goes to protection_failed. At the end it closes file 5 and jumps to $2c60, which sets the IRQ vector to $0969 again and returns to the script.

| <a id="protection_failed"></a>[`protection_failed`](../../../../src/leftovers/leftover_393d.asm#L40) | `$3989` | Protection failed: the script at $1e30 writes 0 to 16000 bytes from $1000 (2 calls of the 8000-byte clear at $1e40: $1000-$4e7f). The script interpreter and the program code are in that range: the program erases itself. |
